title: introduce state sharding for GPU nodepools and IAM-rotation tooling in private installer
author: Priya Nair
description:
Summary: This PR implements a coordinated Terraform state sharding strategy for private deployments that separates GPU nodepool state from VPC/cluster state, and adds an automated IAM-rotation helper used during nodepool lifecycle transitions. Motivation: Private installs have grown hard to operate when multiple teams create ephemeral GPU nodepools in the same TF state workspace. We observed long terraform plan/apply times, repeated terraform lock contention, and operator risk when rolling back pool changes. Separating state for GPU nodepools reduces blast radius, shortens apply times, and makes automated rollback safe. The IAM rotation component provides a controlled mechanism to rotate short-lived credentials and to reconcile nodepool IAM bindings during migration.

What this change does (high level):
- Introduces a new Terraform module layout: terraform/modules/gpu_nodepool with its own state backend configuration helpers and example workspaces.
- Adds a lightweight state-pointer updater (scripts/tfstate-pointer-updater.sh) that migrates a nodepool's resources into the new state file and updates the installer pointer files used by the Private installer.
- Provides an installer-side migrate_state.go (installer/upgrade/migrate_state.go) orchestration that sequences: drain -> terraform import -> state split -> iam rotation -> final verification, and exposes a dry-run flag.
- Adds an IAM-rotation helper (installer/security/iam_rotate.go) that creates short-lived credentials for nodepool controllers, applies new bindings with a canary attach/detach, and validates access before revoking the old key.
- Adds Helm chart hooks and values for running the migrator as a Job during upgrades (installer/helm/charts/gpu/templates/migration-job.yaml and values.yaml knobs).
- E2E tests and unit tests: tests/e2e/private-install-state-migration.test.ts and unit tests under installer/upgrade/* to validate dry-run and rollback behaviors.

Checklist:
- [x] Terraform module and example workspace added
- [x] Migration orchestration implemented with idempotent steps and dry-run
- [x] IAM rotation flows with canary attach/detach validated
- [x] Helm hooks for migration implemented and annotated
- [x] E2E tests for a 1->2 nodepool migration path added
- [x] Integration with CI gating and smoke test added

Compatibility and rollout plan: The migrator is gated behind a feature flag (values.install.migration.enabled=false by default). Operators can opt into migration per-tenant via the installer console. Migration has three safety checkpoints: dry-run, canary attach, and traffic verification. The tfstate-pointer script supports rollback by restoring the original state file if any step fails.

Operational notes for SRE/Operators: the PR includes a step-by-step runbook at terraform/modules/gpu_nodepool/README.md documenting preconditions (backups, lock TTLs), expected downtime (drain + cordon time only), and follow-up verification steps. There is also a lightweight prometheus metric emitted by the migrator job (migrator_last_run_success) and an alert rule suggested in installer/observability/migrator-alerts.yaml.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: accidental double-import or resource orphaning. Mitigation: a built-in plan/preview check that compares resources to be imported and refuses to proceed if diffs exceed a threshold.
- Risk: IAM misbinding during rotation. Mitigation: canary attach/verify before global rollout; automated rollback attaches the previous binding and notifies the operator.
- Risk: terraform state drift post-migration. Mitigation: post-migrate verification step that runs terraform plan against both old and new states and asserts no changes.

Related work: This complements ENG-7834 (tfstate migrations) and builds on the node lifecycle APIs introduced in ENG-7560. The approach intentionally differs from earlier monolithic tfstate migrators by providing per-nodepool workspace isolation and a fast path for revert.

Testing and CI: initial runs showed a transient acceptance test failure in the helm hook ordering when the job precedence race surfaced. Fixes were made (commit a3b4c8) and CI now passes full e2e on the private helm chart matrix. The PR includes a CI job (ci/private-migration-smoke) that can be run manually for large customers before enabling the flag.

Migration example (operator flow, short):
1) Enable values.install.migration.enabled=true for a tenant
2) Run dry-run: ./installer migrate --tenant <T> --nodepool <N> --dry-run
3) Review the generated plan and commit state backup
4) Run actual migrate: ./installer migrate --tenant <T> --nodepool <N>
5) Watch migrator job logs, verify canary attach/traffic, then confirm completion

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the default behavior off. Operators who prefer a full-monolith state can opt to not use the new layout. The migration tooling is designed to be reversible and observable.

Lina Park: A few nit comments on error messages and the terraform import timeout. Can we parameterize the import timeout and expose it in values.yaml?
Priya Nair: Parameterized import timeout and added note about bumping timeouts in large clusters. PTAL.

release_notes: Added state sharding for GPU nodepools and operator tooling for safe migration and IAM rotation. Feature disabled by default; enable via values.install.migration.enabled. See terraform/modules/gpu_nodepool/README.md for operator runbook.
notes_for_ops: Migration is opt-in. Run dry-run, validate plans, backup tfstate, then run migrator. Use ci/private-migration-smoke to validate an environment before enabling in production.
post_merge_tasks: Monitor migrator_last_run_success and migrator_run_id logs; schedule a follow-up to evaluate operator feedback after first 3 migrations. Add a Linear card to track adoption metrics.
